name: Short Box Spread
summary: The reverse box - sell the call spread and the put spread at the same two strikes - receiving cash today and repaying the strike width at expiry; a synthetic borrowing. DANGEROUS on American-style options.
max_profit: (net credit - (K2 - K1)) x 100, i.e. the borrowing benefit - always negative as a standalone P/L; the benefit is the use of the cash
max_loss: UNDEFINED in practice on American options - early assignment on the short ITM leg can force an unwind at an arbitrary loss well beyond the strike width
breakevens: n/a - constant liability of (K2 - K1) at expiry
when_to_use: Never on this system. Institutions use short SPX boxes (European, cash-settled) as cheap financing. On American-style share-settled equity/ETF options the early-assignment path makes it an uncapped risk.
entry_rules: PROHIBITED on this system. American-style, share-settled options make the short box an unbounded-risk borrowing position.
Both short legs are short options; with one ITM by construction, Alpaca will treat parts of it as requiring level 4 in many configurations
Included in the bank only so the automated system can RECOGNIZE and REJECT this shape if a screener ever proposes it
management_rules: Not applicable - blocked at the order-validation layer
exit_rules: If somehow opened: close all four legs immediately, same session, at any reasonable price
Never allow a short ITM leg to sit with extrinsic < $0.05
assignment_risk: Maximum and asymmetric. One short leg is ITM by construction. Assignment converts the box into a naked directional stock position plus three residual legs, exactly the mechanism behind the well-documented retail box-spread losses.
buying_power: Broker-dependent and large; assignment can trigger immediate margin calls.
common_mistakes: Using it as a cheap margin loan on equity options; assuming it behaves like the SPX version.
family: four-leg structures (iron condors, iron butterflies, condors, double calendars/diagonals, boxes, jelly rolls, conversions/reversals, double verticals, double ratio spreads)
blocked_because: needs Alpaca options level 4; this account is level 3. Alpaca rejects it with 'account not eligible to trade uncovered option contracts'. Raising the level is an Alpaca approval, not a code change.
